Sine of the Sum Formula

AreaAlgebraCurves
Game: A diamond sits in a box. Move its four corner triangles around, and the space they leave is two smaller boxes with the same area as the diamond.
How to play: Drag the diamond's right or left corner up and down, and compare the two pictures.

Show
Look for the math

A proof without words by Volker Priebe and Edgar A. Ramos of the sine of a sum, one of the angle sum identities:

sin(α + β) = sin α cos β + cos α sin β

The rhombus

The rhombus has sides of length 1 and touches each side of the rectangle. It cuts off two pairs of equal right triangles with hypotenuse 1: one pair with acute angle α and legs cos α, sin α, the other with β and legs cos β, sin β. The rhombus's angle at its right and left corners is α + β, and a rhombus of side 1 with angle θ has area sin θ. So the rhombus has area sin(α + β).

Moving the triangles

The rectangle is cos α + cos β wide and sin α + sin β tall. Put the two α triangles together into a cos α × sin α box in one corner, and the two β triangles into a cos β × sin β box in the opposite corner. What is left is two boxes, sin α × cos β and cos α × sin β. The same triangles were taken from the same rectangle both times, so the leftover areas are equal: that is the formula.

What was checked

The logic test built both pictures for all 7,921 pairs of whole-degree angles from 1° to 89°. It checked that the rhombus has four sides of length 1 and angle α + β, that the moved triangles are the same triangles and fill two corners exactly, and that the two areas agree every time. That includes angles with α + β over 90°.

Make the rhombus a square (α + β = 90°). What happens to the two empty boxes?
